conviction_note: Nothing decisive: a revenue build from the company's own Q4 segment table points to Q1 revenue modestly above the ~$265-267M consensus. But this name sold a 14% revenue beat last quarter (-5.5%), the EPS bar is disputed, and the negatives are known (legacy beer -17%, BrewDog cash burn, ATM and note-exchange dilution). With 14% of float short and upside skew paid, I lean slightly up: p_up 53 on an abs move of 9 (below the 10.5 implied, because the last three prints moved 1-5%). impact_sum +0.8 and scaled +0.54 agree in sign and scale.
bar: Revenue $264.9M for Q1 FY27, EPS -$0.18, from Earnings Whispers preview 2026-09-30 (https://earningswhispers.com/article/TLRY/20307). A second search-aggregated figure gives revenue $267.2M and EPS -$0.01 (source page not identified; benzinga/marketbeat family). The revenue bar agrees across the two to within 1%. The EPS bar is DISPUTED (-$0.01 vs -$0.18), so the EPS line is unsourced and the findings are capped small. Company guide: FY27 adj EBITDA $68-75M and 'over $1 billion' FY27 revenue (Q4 FY26 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1731348/000117184326004944/exh_991.htm; https://beerinsights.com/archive-article/60482). No quarterly guide. Q1 FY26 comps: revenue $209.5M, adj EBITDA $10.2M.
positioning_check: Short interest 14.38% of float, 5.2 days to cover, record date 2026-09-15 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/TLRY/short-interest, via sweep row). Baseline 25d skew -4.36 vol points, so upside is paid, put/call OI 0.76, and the baseline reads 'upside paid'. Event-implied move 10.54% (ATM spread 40% of mid, indicative only). Spot $3.74 is 4.8% above the 52-week low and 82% off the high; 20-day run-up -11.2%. The stock was $4.88 on 2026-08-26 (Form 4 withholding price) and exchanged notes at about $4.22 in early September. Earnings Whispers says bullish sentiment fell from 7.4% to 3.4% ahead of the print. A crowded-ish short sits at the lows with call skew bid, so the negatives are shrunk.

findings.finding: A revenue build from the company's own segment numbers points to Q1 FY27 revenue of about $272-285M against a $264.9-267.2M consensus. Q4 FY26 segments: cannabis $71.5M (+5% YoY), beverage $105.6M (+61%, of which BrewDog $51.1M for about 3 months from 2 March), distribution $85.0M (+15%), wellness $19.7M (+16%). The Q1 FY26 base was $209.5M (cannabis $64.5M, beverage $55.7M, about $89M distribution plus wellness). Q1 FY27 gets the first full summer quarter of BrewDog (management: 'over $200M annual' run-rate) and the Lyphe UK clinic acquisition (April 2026). Netting legacy beer at -15% still gives roughly +3-7% over the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-07-28): revenue $281.7M against $246.3M estimate (+14%) with an EPS miss, and the stock fell 5.5% on the day (https://247wallst.com/companies/tlry/earnings/; baseline -0.99% close-to-close). Q1 FY26 (2025-10-09): a revenue beat of $209.5M against $205.75M plus an EPS beat gave +22%. Revenue beats alone have not been paid recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $265M is only +26% YoY, about BrewDog alone added to a flat base, while the Q4 run-rate ex-BrewDog grew 2.7% and distribution and wellness grew mid-teens. If the market had priced a revenue beat, the stock would not be sitting 4.8% off its 52-week low. But this name does not pay for revenue, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Same company document as the BrewDog cash finding. Management's 'annualized pro forma run rate of approximately $1.2 billion' (Q4 call summary, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-tilray-inc-stock/) implies about $300M a quarter, above consensus. This is an inference, not a reported number.

findings.finding: Legacy US craft beer revenue fell about 17% organically last quarter, and Tilray stopped beer production at its Terrapin brewery (Athens, GA) from 2026-09-25, moving brewing to other US plants. That is ongoing erosion in about 20% of revenue plus a restructuring that will show up as charges and possibly as cost-savings language on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no isolated reaction to the beverage line. Q4 FY26 beverage +61% (BrewDog) did not lift the stock (-5.5% on the day).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the -17% is in the preview copy and the Terrapin closure was public in September. What is not priced is the size of the Q1 legacy decline and any savings quantified on the call.
findings.independence: Terrapin closure from a separate search summary of September 2026 Tilray news (finviz announcement page, https://finviz.com/news/395595/tilray-brands-to-announce-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results-on-october-8-2026 surfaced alongside it). A proxy is the UK craft category at -1.3% MAT (https://catererlicensee.com/world-cup-and-summer-heat-drive-strongest-month-of-2026-for-uk-pubs-and-bars/).

findings.finding: Share count rose from 136.2M (10-K cover, 2026-07-24) to 147.8M (DEF 14A record date, 2026-09-24), +8.5% in two months. Debt-for-equity exchanges account for about 4.2M of it (1.38M shares for $6M and 2.84M for $12M of 5.20% 2027 converts, 8-Ks of 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-14) and PSU vesting for about 1-1.5M. The rest is consistent with the $180M ATM opened 2026-04-15. What the money buys: retiring 2027 notes and funding BrewDog's revival (about £50M invested, 16 bars reopened). Cash was $235M at year-end with net debt under $1M, so this is not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean reaction. ATM dilution has run through 2026 while the stock fell about 47% YTD by August (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/19/tilray-jumps-6-canopy-growth-climbs-3-aurora-cannabis-gains-4-heres-why-tlry-is-still-down-47-ytd/).
findings.why_not_priced: The share counts are public in the 10-K and the proxy, but nobody aggregates the gap. Per-share EPS and the ATM pace in Q1 get disclosed in the 10-Q. If it were fully priced, the selling would have stopped; the stock is still at the lows. Financing funds a visible reinvestment (BrewDog bars reopened), so the sign is only mildly negative.

findings.finding: Tilray has put almost £50M into BrewDog since buying it for £33M (operations, working capital, staff, growth infrastructure), reopened 16 bars and launched its first big marketing push. The CEO says BrewDog is expected to be cash-flow positive only in (calendar) 2027. Q1 FY27 therefore carries BrewDog investment and probably negative adjusted free cash flow and pressure on beverage margin. Q4 beverage gross margin was 38%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26: adj EBITDA $31.9M (+15%) but an EPS miss, and the stock fell 5.5%. FY26 adjusted FCF -$86M. Earnings quality has been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The £50M figure ran in UK trade press (Grocery Gazette, press release on finviz), not in US equity previews, which focus on BrewDog revenue. If it were priced, previews would flag Q1 cash burn and consensus EBITDA would sit below the run-rate. BrewDog is about 20% of revenue; the rest (distribution +15%, international cannabis +20%+) can offset it.
findings.independence: CEO's 'cash flow positive in 2027' quote, City AM 2026-04-16 (https://www.cityam.com/brewdog-can-be-worth-1bn-new-owner-says/). Company release relay: https://finviz.com/news/394104/brewdog-launches-under-new-ownership-campaign-marking-a-new-era-of-fresh-energy-new-backing-and-award-winning-beer.

findings.finding: UK on-trade, the core BrewDog channel in its first full summer under Tilray: July 2026 draught volumes +3.9% YoY and rate of sale +5.2% (World Cup plus heat), 'one of the strongest trading months of 2026'. Late August turned weak (bank-holiday pints -3.9% YoY in rain) and craft was -1.3% MAT.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line; BrewDog has been consolidated for only one quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: UK pub-industry data (Vianet/Oxford Partnership) is not in US cannabis-stock previews. It is a proxy for one channel of one segment, sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The bank-holiday decline cuts the other way (https://catererlicensee.com/busier-pubs-and-longer-visits-fail-to-lift-summer-bank-holiday-pint-sales/).

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Tilray point to continued German medical cannabis demand. Aurora's international medical revenue for the quarter to 2026-06-30 rose 17% YoY to C$43.3M, 'mainly due to higher sales in Germany driven by increased patient demand'. BfArM data show German flower imports in Q1 2026 at 67.6t, +37% YoY. Tilray's international cannabis (Q4 $27.2M) grew 20%+ for three straight quarters but absorbed $21.1M of price compression in FY26.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International growth was cited in every recent print with muted reactions (-1%, -5%, +0.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: A peer print that landed after Tilray last spoke. Partly priced, because the international story is known. Germany's pending MedCanG reform (a telemedicine and mail-order ban, not yet passed per the search) caps the read-through.
findings.independence: BfArM import data via StratCann (https://stratcann.com/news/canada-supplied-half-germanys-cannabis-imports-in-q1-2026/). The Aurora document is primary for the peer.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-20 Tilray raised global annual medical cannabis cultivation capacity from 210 to 275 tonnes (Quebec expansion plus the EU-GMP site in Portugal), citing international demand. Management had called supply availability and permit timing the binding constraints on international growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the announcement day the stock fell 0.9% (goldesel).
findings.why_not_priced: It got no reaction when announced. It matters only if the call ties it to higher international volume in the FY27 guide; Quebec EU-GMP is about 12 months away, so it is mostly forward.
findings.independence: Q4 call summary on supply as the constraint (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-tilray-inc-stock/).

findings.finding: Veterans Affairs Canada cut medical cannabis reimbursement rates about 30% from 2026-04-01 (Aurora's Q1 FY27 release blames it for a Canadian medical margin fall from 69% to 61%). Tilray's Canadian medical revenue is small ($5.4M in Q4), so the hit to its quarter is minor.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and partly in Q4 already (Mar-May). It is in the price at this size.
findings.independence: Shares the Aurora document with the German-demand finding. Canopy also cites the VAC cut (https://finviz.com/news/379357/canopy-growth-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results-delivers-13-net-revenue-growth-with-contributions-from-all-businesses).

findings.finding: The federal intoxicating-hemp ban (THC limited to under 0.4mg per container) takes effect 2026-11-13; a Senate CR proposal would push it to 2026-12-11, and bills seek two- to three-year delays. Tilray sells hemp-derived THC drinks in the US, so the FY27 guide and the call may have to address lost hemp revenue.
findings.source_date: 2026 (page undated in snippet; the effective date is from the November 2025 funding law)
findings.why_not_priced: Industry-wide and known. Whether Tilray quantifies its exposure on the call is the only new part. The ban itself takes effect after the window; only the call commentary is inside.

findings.finding: Positioning: 14.38% of float short (5.2 days to cover, 2026-09-15), stock 4.8% above its 52-week low after -11% in 20 days, 25d skew -4.36 (calls bid), and preview sentiment at 3.4% bullish. An in-line print with the FY27 EBITDA guide reaffirmed meets a short base and a washed-out tape.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-09 print: +22% on a modest beat into a beaten-down tape. The last three prints were muted (-1%, -5%, +0.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is what the price is, not something it has missed. The asymmetry is that downside news (legacy beer, dilution) is in the preview copy while the stock sits at the lows. Sized small.
findings.independence: Sentiment drop from Earnings Whispers (https://earningswhispers.com/article/TLRY/20307); skew from the sealed baseline.

outside_window.finding: The DEA's broader marijuana rescheduling (hearing 2026-06-29 to 07-15) still awaits the ALJ's recommended decision and then the Administrator's final rule, with no deadline. Any ruling could move TLRY as a sentiment name, but nothing ties it to the 2026-10-08 window.
The federal hemp-THC ban takes effect 2026-11-13 (possibly delayed to 2026-12-11). Only the call commentary on it falls inside the window and is filed above.
The Carlsberg US production and distribution licence starts in January 2027 (10-K).

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees: a slight upside lean matches the paid call skew (-4.36) and the oversold 20-day run-up (-11%), and the known negatives (dilution, legacy beer, BrewDog burn) are what the tape has already been selling.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction): revenue-build finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6, because last quarter's 14% revenue beat traded -5.5%
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the dilution finding went from -0.4 to -0.2 once I asked what the money buys (2027 note retirement, BrewDog reinvestment, net debt under $1M), so it is not distress
Rule 7 (positioning): with 14.4% of float short and calls bid, the BrewDog cash-burn negative went from -0.5 to -0.4
Rule 6 (bar): the EPS bar is disputed (-$0.01 vs -$0.18), so the findings stay capped small and the revenue bar from two roughly agreeing sources is used for print_vs_bar
Rule 5 (proxies): the UK pub and German peer findings stay small and are labelled as proxies; nothing was dropped
